content.text:
Overdue notices now say how many days late the item is, for example "It is 5 days late." All 60 tests pass, including a new one for this.

- **Wording:** the overdue template in `lib/notices/templates.js` now reads: `Hello {name}, "{title}" was due back on {dueOn}. It is {daysLate} late. Please return it to any branch.`
- **Day count:** `overdueNotices` in `lib/notices/digest.js` works out the days with `daysBetween(loan.dueOn, today)`. It passes the result to the template as "5 days", or "1 day" when it's one day, so it never says "1 days".
- **Test:** `test/notices.test.js` checks one loan that is 1 day late and one that is 5 days late.

I didn't count grace days. `GRACE_DAYS` in `lib/fees/schedule.js` only affects fees, so a notice counts days from the due date. Say if you'd rather it subtract the grace period.

result:
Overdue notices now say how many days late the item is, for example "It is 5 days late." All 60 tests pass, including a new one for this.

- **Wording:** the overdue template in `lib/notices/templates.js` now reads: `Hello {name}, "{title}" was due back on {dueOn}. It is {daysLate} late. Please return it to any branch.`
- **Day count:** `overdueNotices` in `lib/notices/digest.js` works out the days with `daysBetween(loan.dueOn, today)`. It passes the result to the template as "5 days", or "1 day" when it's one day, so it never says "1 days".
- **Test:** `test/notices.test.js` checks one loan that is 1 day late and one that is 5 days late.

I didn't count grace days. `GRACE_DAYS` in `lib/fees/schedule.js` only affects fees, so a notice counts days from the due date. Say if you'd rather it subtract the grace period.
